overview: Hera is a Legendary Support of the Starglint faction built around a dual-axis control identity: she simultaneously neutralizes the most dangerous enemy carry and amplifies the friendliest carry. No other support in the current roster does both at once.

Her Ultimate, Tide of Obsession, charms the nearest enemy and forces them to attack their own team - turning the opposing DPS into a liability. Her Skill 2, Fatal Infatuation, marks the highest-damage enemy with an Obsession debuff that locks them out of attacking entirely and pulls them toward Hera while dealing DoT. Her Skill 1, Crown's Bestowal, simultaneously buffs the friendly hero with the highest ATK with both ATK and ATK Speed.

Her passive, Royal Domain, places a field over the friendly half at battle start. Inside it, Hera regenerates Energy faster and gains stacking damage reduction - making her naturally harder to burst down early, which is critical for a unit whose value comes from completing multiple control cycles.

The CN community describes her as a stronger, modernized variant of Pan - a control-focused support whose ceiling rises sharply with Relic investment, particularly at Relic Lv3. Official release: 18 February 2026 on CN server.
All ratings and strategic assessments are based on CN server skill data and early community analysis (TapTap CN). Data current as of March 2026. Numerical stats are not available in this guide.

lore.label: Queen of Olympus - Greek Mythology
lore.intro: Hera is the queen of the Olympian gods in Greek mythology - goddess of marriage, family, and sovereign power. Wife and sister of Zeus, she is famous for her fierce jealousy, her dominion over the fates of heroes and enemies alike, and her absolute authority over those within her domain. The game draws directly on these themes for her mechanical identity.
bullets: Tide of Obsession mirrors Hera's mythological weaponization of madness and desire - she famously drove heroes to ruin by bending their minds against them
Fatal Infatuation reflects her role as the goddess who draws enemies inward and claims them, pulling the threat that poses the greatest danger into her orbit
Crown's Bestowal represents her sovereign authority to crown and elevate - Hera grants her chosen champion the power of a king
Royal Domain embodies her claim over Olympus itself: within her half of the battlefield, her authority is absolute and her power is amplified
The Relic, Charm Seal, is her brand of ownership - enemies she has controlled bear her mark and are left permanently weakened in their resistance to her

coreMechanic.sectionTitle: Core Mechanic - The Charm Control Loop
coreMechanic.label: How Hera's Control Chain Works
bullets: Hera has two distinct control states she applies: Charm from her Ultimate, and Obsession from Fatal Infatuation. Both are covered by her Relic.

Charm: The charmed target attacks its own allies. Hera's Ultimate also boosts the charmed target's normal attack damage - making the most powerful auto-attacker on the enemy team the most dangerous weapon pointed at themselves.

Obsession: The obsessed target cannot attack at all, moves slower, and is continuously pulled toward Hera. It takes DoT while Hera heals herself for the same amount. This is a hard anti-carry disable, not just a redirection.
Charm Seal (Relic): Enemies who have been under either Charm or Obsession lose Effect Resistance permanently for the rest of the fight. This makes all subsequent control attempts more reliable.

Relic Lv3 is the critical breakpoint: charmed enemies can no longer gain Energy. This converts Charm from a simple redirection into Control + Energy Denial - the charmed carry cannot build toward their own Ultimate while they fight their teammates.
Relic Lv4: If the charmed unit kills an ally during the Charm duration, the Charm is extended. The more dangerous the charmed target, the longer the effect persists.

highlightBox.label: Internal Kit Synergy
bullets: Crown's Bestowal buffs the friendly carry with the highest ATK - while Fatal Infatuation simultaneously locks down the opposing carry with the highest damage output. One cast covers both flanks.
Tide of Obsession charms a third target and redirects their auto-attacks, creating a three-vector control state: friendly carry boosted, enemy carry locked, second enemy turned on their own team.
Royal Domain provides passive Energy regeneration that accelerates Hera's own Ultimate cycle - the longer the fight, the faster she rotates through her control chain.
Hera's kit does not fight against itself. Each piece reinforces the same goal: protect your carry, neutralize their carry, and convert enemy aggression into self-inflicted damage.

skills.name: Tide of Obsession
skills.description: Hera releases a wave of Charm toward the nearest enemy. The struck enemy is Charmed and attacks their own allies. While Charmed, the target's normal attack damage is boosted.

upgrades.text: The charmed target's normal attack damage bonus is increased further.
The charmed target's normal attack damage bonus is increased further.

skills.note: The boosted normal attack damage is the key detail: Hera does not just disable a threat, she amplifies it and redirects it. The stronger the enemy auto-attacker, the more damage their own team absorbs during the Charm duration. Works most devastatingly against teams with a dominant auto-attack carry.

skills.name: Charm Seal
skills.description: Enemies who have been under Hera's Charm or Obsession control have their Effect Resistance reduced.

upgrades.text: Charmed enemies also receive Crown's Bestowal (ATK/ATK Speed buff applied to the enemy carry).
Charmed enemies cannot gain Energy for the duration of the Charm.
If the charmed enemy kills an ally during the Charm, the Charm duration is extended.

skills.note: Relic Lv3 is Hera's most important investment threshold. Adding Energy Denial to Charm converts a strong CC effect into a strategic shutdown: the charmed carry cannot build toward their own Ultimate while damaging their allies. Lv4 creates a self-sustaining loop if the charmed unit is strong enough to actually secure kills.

skills.name: Crown's Bestowal
skills.description: Hera grants her crown to the friendly hero with the highest ATK, increasing their ATK and ATK Speed for a duration.
skills.note: Auto-targeting means no manual carry designation is needed: the highest-ATK ally always receives the buff. Build your team's carry to have the highest ATK and the crown reliably lands on the correct target every cycle. The ATK Speed component makes this particularly valuable for heroes whose output scales with attack frequency.

skills.name: Fatal Infatuation
skills.description: Targets the enemy dealing the highest damage and applies Obsession: the target cannot attack, moves slower, and is gradually pulled toward Hera. The target takes DoT equal to a percentage of Hera's ATK per second. Hera heals herself for the same amount.

upgrades.text: DoT per second is increased further.

skills.note: This is an unconditional hard-disable against the opposing team's most threatening damage source. Unlike Charm, Obsession does not redirect the target - it simply removes them from the fight entirely for its duration while restoring Hera's HP.

skills.name: Royal Domain
skills.description: At battle start, Hera deploys a Power Field over the friendly half of the battlefield. Inside the field, Hera regenerates Energy faster and gains stacking Damage Reduction (up to a cap). When enemies first enter the field, they are Suppressed.

upgrades.text: Damage reduction inside the field is increased.
Suppression duration on enemy entry is extended.
When Hera would take fatal damage, she withdraws the field, becomes briefly immune, and heals a percentage of her Max HP.

skills.note: Royal Domain is Hera's durability engine. The Energy regeneration bonus accelerates her Ultimate cycle, ensuring she completes multiple Charm rotations in a single fight. Lv4 provides a pseudo-revival - a last-resort survival window rather than a passive sustain tool.

skillUpgradePriority: 1. Charm Seal (Relic) - Lv3 Energy Denial is the most impactful breakpoint in Hera's entire kit; prioritize Relic investment above all else
2. Fatal Infatuation (Skill 2) - The hard anti-carry disable; Lv3 duration extension significantly increases the window the opposing carry is removed from the fight
3. Tide of Obsession (Ultimate) - More Charm duration and higher redirected damage at higher levels; primary control tool
4. Royal Domain (Passive) - Lv4 pseudo-revival is valuable as insurance; Lv3 extended Suppression improves field control
5. Crown's Bestowal (Skill 1) - Strong carry buff, but lower priority than the control skills that define Hera's kit

ratings.desc: Anti-carry targeting, Charm redirection, Energy Denial via Relic Lv3 - oppressive against single-carry compositions
Strong carry buff and control provide consistent value; team-dependent in content where enemies resist or ignore CC
Control and self-sustain via Royal Domain support extended multi-stage fights; value depends on content's CC susceptibility
Crown's Bestowal adds carry support value; core CC identity diminished when targets are immune to Charm and Obsession

paragraphs: Hera should be placed in a protected backline position. Her Royal Domain automatically covers the friendly half, meaning she benefits from its Energy regeneration and damage reduction regardless of her exact position within it. Her Skill targeting is auto-directed - no manual positioning is required to hit the correct targets.

Keeping Hera alive through multiple control cycles is the primary constraint. Each subsequent cast of Fatal Infatuation and Tide of Obsession applies the Charm Seal debuff again, reducing Effect Resistance further. More cycles = more reliable control = more value extracted from the Relic investment.
Front: Tank or taunt unit (Momus recommended by CN community) - absorbs initial burst and establishes the first control interaction that Hera compounds on.

Mid: Your highest-ATK carry - Crown's Bestowal will target them automatically. Build this hero for ATK to guarantee consistent targeting. Pan or a second CC unit can fill the fourth slot to extend control chains.
Back: Hera + healing support. Hera's self-heal from Fatal Infatuation provides partial sustain, but a dedicated healer (Yuelao, Cancer) significantly improves her survival in long fights.

strengths: Dual-axis control: simultaneously buffs friendly carry (Crown's Bestowal) and disables enemy carry (Fatal Infatuation) in the same rotation
Charm redirection converts the most dangerous enemy auto-attacker into a source of friendly fire - value scales with the strength of the charmed target
Royal Domain provides passive Energy regeneration, enabling faster Ultimate cycles than most supports without external Energy support
Charm Seal Relic stacks Effect Resistance reduction after each control event, making all subsequent CC more reliable as the fight progresses
Relic Lv3 adds Energy Denial to Charm - a hard counter to Ultimate-dependent enemy carries
Self-heal from Fatal Infatuation provides partial sustain without requiring a dedicated healer slot
Royal Domain Lv4 pseudo-revival acts as a survival safety net equivalent in concept to Skadi's Relic Lv2
CN community rates her as a stronger, more modern variant of Pan - indicating high competitive ceiling
weaknesses: Heavily gated by Relic investment - considered significantly stronger at Relic Lv3 and above; weaker at low investment levels
Charm and Obsession both fail against high Effect Resistance targets, CC-immune enemies, or Cleanse abilities
Value drops sharply against multi-carry or balanced teams without a dominant single DPS to disable
Crown's Bestowal requires the team to have a clear highest-ATK carry to benefit - unfocused team builds dilute the buff
Boss and PvE content with CC-immune enemies strips most of her kit value, leaving only the carry buff
Burst compositions that eliminate Hera before she completes a second control cycle prevent the Charm Seal stack from compounding
Still early meta: exact Relic breakpoints and dupe value remain under-documented (data as of March 2026)

entries.name: Momus
entries.text: The CN community's primary recommended partner (source: TapTap, Feb/March 2026). Momus's AoE Taunt creates the first CC state on the frontline, which Hera's Charm then layers on top. The combination leaves the opposing team with no safe attack target: taunted units cannot stop attacking Momus, charmed units attack their own allies. Also functions as the primary tank protecting Hera's backline position.

entries.name: Hladgunnr (Swan)
entries.text: The natural Crown's Bestowal target in most compositions: high ATK value ensures she reliably receives the buff, and she benefits significantly from both the ATK multiplier and the ATK Speed component. Her burst payloads land into windows that Hera's Charm and Obsession create, where the opposing team is either attacking themselves or locked out of responding.

entries.name: Pan
entries.text: AoE CC partner that chains directly with Hera's single-target control. Pan's silence and daze extend the windows enemies spend unable to act, compounding with Charm Seal's accumulated Effect Resistance reduction. CN community references a "Hera + Momus" CC chain composition that could equivalently substitute Pan for the AoE CC layer.

entries.name: Yuelao
entries.text: Healing support that covers Hera's partial self-sustain and extends her survivability between control cycles. The CN "san-xiang-dui" (three-item team) composition specifically pairs Hera with Yuelao and Cancer as the healing core. Keeping Hera alive into the third or fourth control rotation extracts the full compounding value of the Charm Seal Effect Resistance reduction.

entries.name: Caishen
entries.text: Team-wide Energy acceleration compounds with Hera's Royal Domain Energy regeneration. More Energy means faster Ultimate rotations, which means faster Charm cycles and more Charm Seal stacks in the same fight window. In sustained compositions, Caishen can create near-constant Ultimate availability across the team.

entries.name: Mengpo
entries.text: Revival stacks directly with Hera's Royal Domain Lv4 pseudo-revival for double insurance. Longer fights compound Hera's Charm Seal stacks further - and Mengpo's Lycoris Bloom may target Hera if she leads in Energy inside her Royal Domain, providing additional ATK% on top of her damage reduction. Recommended for sustained PVE compositions.

playstyle: Hera plays as a dual-axis control support - a hero whose value comes not from healing, shielding, or raw output, but from simultaneous offensive and defensive manipulation. In the opening phase, Royal Domain is already active: Hera is passively accelerating her Energy regeneration and stacking damage reduction before a single skill fires.

The core rotation executes simultaneously on both flanks: Crown's Bestowal finds the friendly carry and boosts them; Fatal Infatuation finds the opposing carry and removes them; Tide of Obsession charms a third target and turns their attacks against their own team. In a single rotation, Hera has buffed the most important friendly unit, disabled the most dangerous enemy unit, and created a source of friendly fire within the opposing team.

The Relic is not optional for competitive play. At Relic Lv1, Hera reduces Effect Resistance on controlled targets - meaningful but not decisive. At Relic Lv3, the charmed carry cannot gain Energy during the Charm window. That changes the role entirely: Hera is no longer just redirecting a threat, she is denying them the resources to respond with their own Ultimate. Each subsequent Charm rotation compounds this advantage through accumulated Charm Seal stacks.

The critical investment question is Relic Lv3. Below it, Hera is a strong but beatable support. At it, the CN community considers her among the most oppressive control tools in PVP - particularly effective against Isis-centric auto-attack compositions where her Charm creates maximum friendly fire and her Relic blocks the Energy cycle that keeps Isis online.
